transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I came in because my family and friends made me. They keep showing me these bank papers and saying it proves that nothing was taken from me. But... for over a year now, I’ve known they’re hiding my money. 

They just use all these things to cover it up, you know? Like saying they have bills to pay, or setting up fundraisers, or making plans for trips. It's all just a cover. So I have to keep confronting them about it. I'm just going to keep at it until they finally tell the truth.
Besides noticing that your money is being hidden, have you heard voices or seen things that other people around you don't seem to hear or see?

No, I don't hear any voices or anything like that. And I don't see things that aren't there. I'm not... I'm not making things up in my head, if that's what you're asking. I just know what they're doing with my money, because it's happening right in front of me. I don't need to hear voices to figure that out.
Do your family members and friends actually believe that your money is being hidden, or do they think this isn't really happening?

No, they say it isn't happening. They keep showing me those same bank papers, saying it proves nothing was taken from me. But... I mean, for over a year now I've known they're hiding my money. They just use all their bills, or those fundraisers, or trip plans to cover it up. So they definitely don't admit it. That's why I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth.

If your family members showed you additional evidence or documentation that your money is actually safe and hasn't been taken, would that change your mind about what's happening, or do you think they would just be creating more false evidence to cover things up?

No, it wouldn't change my mind. Any new papers they show me... it's just going to be more fake proof. I've already told you, they keep showing me bank statements and saying it proves nothing was taken, but I know what's going on. I've known for over a year. They're hiding my money and using all their bills, the fundraisers, the trips... it's all just a cover-up. So, no, more papers won't change anything. I'm just going to keep confronting them until they finally admit the truth.
Do you think it's possible that you might be mistaken about your family hiding your money, or are you completely certain this is definitely happening?

I'm completely certain. There's no way I'm mistaken about this. Like I said, I came in because my family and friends keep trying to tell me that nothing is happening. They keep pointing at those bank papers, saying it proves my money wasn't taken. But I've known for over a year now that they are hiding it. They just use their bills and those fundraisers and trip plans to cover up what they're doing. I know what's going on, and I'm going to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth.

Besides the money being hidden by your family, do you have beliefs about other things happening to you - like people following you, your thoughts being controlled, or conspiracies involving other groups of people or organizations?

No, nothing like that. Nobody's following me, and nobody is controlling my thoughts or anything weird like that. It's just... it's just my family and friends hiding my money. That's the only thing happening. There aren't any big conspiracies or other groups involved, just them taking my money and covering it up with their expenses.

Have you noticed anything else unusual or suspicious happening - like feeling that people have special feelings toward you, or believing you have special abilities or importance, or suspecting that someone is being unfaithful to you?

No, nothing like that. I don't think I have any special powers or anything, and I don't think anyone is in love with me from afar. I'm not worried about anyone cheating on me, either. It's really just the money. That's the only thing going on. My family is hiding my money, and that's what I'm focused on. There's nothing else unusual happening.

When your family shows you those bank statements and says nothing was taken, do you ever wonder if maybe - even just for a moment - there's any chance they could actually be right and you might be wrong about the money being hidden?

No, I don't. I don't wonder if they're right, because they're not. I mean, I know we've talked about this, but that's exactly why I'm here. They just keep waving those bank papers in my face, telling me it proves nothing was taken. But I've known for over a year that they're hiding my money. They just use their regular bills, or talk about fundraisers, or make up these trip plans to cover it all up. So, no, there's no chance I'm wrong. I'm just going to keep confronting them until they finally admit what they're doing and tell the truth.
Do you think it's possible that your mind might be playing tricks on you about the money, or do you believe with absolute certainty that your family is definitely hiding it from you?

No, my mind isn't playing tricks on me. I am absolutely certain. I know I just said this, but I came in here because they keep telling me those bank papers prove nothing was taken. But I've known for over a year now that they are hiding my money. They just use their regular bills, or say they're doing fundraisers, or talk about trip plans to cover it all up. I'm not crazy, I just have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth.
Have you ever talked to a doctor or mental health professional before about these concerns with your family hiding your money?

No, I haven't. I've never seen a psychiatrist or a therapist or anyone like that before. I didn't think I needed to, because I'm not the one with the problem. They're the ones lying and stealing from me. I only came here because they kept pushing me to, saying I'm being unreasonable and that I need help. But I don't need help, I just need my money back. So, no, this is the first time I'm talking to a doctor about it.

When you think about your family hiding your money, do you believe they're doing this for a specific reason - like they want the money for themselves - or do you think there's a bigger reason or pattern behind why they're doing this to you?

I don't know. I really don't know why they're doing it. I mean... I guess they just want the money for themselves? I haven't figured out if there's some big reason or anything like that. 

I just know that they're hiding it from me. It doesn't make any sense why my own family would treat me like this, but... they are. I don't really care about the reason why at this point. I just want them to stop lying and give it back.

Over this past year, besides the money being hidden, have there been any other situations where you felt certain that something was happening, but when you looked back on it later, you realized you might have been wrong about what was going on?

No, I haven't had anything like that happen. I mean, I don't really have moments where I look back and think I was wrong about something big. Everything else in my life is just... normal, I guess. It's really just this thing with my family and the money. I'm not confused about other things, and I haven't been wrong about this, either.
In your work or daily activities outside of this money situation, do you ever feel strongly convinced about something that others around you disagree with or say isn't true?

No, not at all. Like I said, everything else is just normal. I don't really do much since I'm not working right now, but when I'm out doing errands or talking to people, we don't argue about things like that. I don't go around making things up or getting into disagreements with everyone. It's literally just my family and my money. That's the only thing.

When your family talks about their bills, or their fundraisers, or their trip plans, do you feel like they're specifically talking about these things to send you a message or to let you know something about what they're doing with your money?

Well, they're not sending me a secret message or anything. They're just using those things to cover it up. 

My family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but... I've known for over a year now that they're hiding my money. So when they talk about paying their bills, or doing these fundraisers, or planning trips, that's just their way of covering up where the money is really coming from. 

That's why I'm here, honestly. I just have to keep confronting them about it until they finally tell the truth. They can show me all the bank papers they want, but I know what they're doing and I'm not going to stop asking them until they admit it.

When you first started believing that your family was hiding your money a year ago, did this belief come on suddenly - like you woke up one day and just knew it - or did it develop gradually over time as you noticed more and more things that seemed suspicious?

I don't really remember exactly how it started, to be honest. It wasn't like a sudden thing where I just woke up and knew. I don't really know if it was gradual either. I just know that they have it. It's been over a year, so I don't remember the very first day I figured it out. I just know that it's happening.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if there are other situations where the patient holds a strong conviction that others disagree with (exploring other potential delusions). The symptom profile only mentions the specific delusion about family/friends hiding money, but does not provide information about whether the patient has other strong convictions in work or daily activities that others disagree with.

patient.answer: No, not at all. Like I said, everything else is just normal. I don't really do much since I'm not working right now, but when I'm out doing errands or talking to people, we don't argue about things like that. I don't go around making things up or getting into disagreements with everyone. It's literally just my family and my money. That's the only thing.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusion is confined to the money/family situation (F22.9 - delusional disorder, unspecified) or if there are pervasive themes of reference, persecution, or control that suggest a more systematized delusional disorder (F22.0 - erotomanic, grandiose, jealous, persecutory, or somatic type). Specifically, I need to clarify if the patient experiences ideas of reference - feeling that neutral events, conversations, or actions by others are directed at them or have special meaning related to the money situation.
doctor.question: When your family talks about their bills, or their fundraisers, or their trip plans, do you feel like they're specifically talking about these things to send you a message or to let you know something about what they're doing with your money?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's belief that her family is using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover up hiding her money, which relates directly to the manifestation of her delusions (S019).

patient.answer:
Well, they're not sending me a secret message or anything. They're just using those things to cover it up. 

My family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but... I've known for over a year now that they're hiding my money. So when they talk about paying their bills, or doing these fundraisers, or planning trips, that's just their way of covering up where the money is really coming from. 

That's why I'm here, honestly. I just have to keep confronting them about it until they finally tell the truth. They can show me all the bank papers they want, but I know what they're doing and I'm not going to stop asking them until they admit it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a primary delusional belief (F22.0) versus a delusional disorder that developed in context of a relationship or specific stressor (F22.9), by assessing whether the delusion arose suddenly or gradually, and whether there was a clear precipitating event.
doctor.question: When you first started believing that your family was hiding your money a year ago, did this belief come on suddenly - like you woke up one day and just knew it - or did it develop gradually over time as you noticed more and more things that seemed suspicious?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the onset of the delusion (whether it was sudden or gradual), which is not covered by any of the symptom profile items (which cover the nature of the delusion, functioning, impairment, and duration, but not the speed/manner of onset).

patient.answer: I don't really remember exactly how it started, to be honest. It wasn't like a sudden thing where I just woke up and knew. I don't really know if it was gradual either. I just know that they have it. It's been over a year, so I don't remember the very first day I figured it out. I just know that it's happening.

inference.note: Patient demonstrates a non-bizarre, circumscribed delusional belief (money being hidden) that has persisted for over a year. Key features supporting F22.0 (Delusional disorder, erotomanic type) rule-out and F22.9 (Delusional disorder, unspecified) confirmation: (1) No hallucinations present; (2) Functioning relatively preserved outside the delusional content; (3) Belief is non-bizarre and plausible in content (money theft); (4) Absolute conviction despite contradictory evidence (bank statements); (5) No ideas of reference or special significance attributed to family's communications; (6) No other psychotic features; (7) Duration >1 month (actually >1 year); (8) Unable to recall sudden onset, suggesting gradual development. This is classic delusional disorder, unspecified type (F22.9), as the delusion does not fit the specific subtypes (erotomanic, grandiose, jealous, persecutory, somatic). F22.0 (erotomanic) is ruled out as there is no romantic/love-based delusional content.

opening_question.intent: Establish rapport and identify the chief complaint that brings the patient to the clinic today
opening_question.question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a non-bizarre, circumscribed delusional belief (money being hidden by family) that has persisted for over one year without prominent hallucinations or other psychotic features. The belief is held with absolute conviction despite contradictory evidence (bank statements), meets criteria for a primary delusional disorder, and the patient has no prior psychiatric history. The absence of hallucinations, mood episodes, substance use, or general medical conditions supports Delusional Disorder rather than Brief Psychotic Disorder or other psychotic disorders.
